First, I've got a sort of amusing anecdote about such a situation.

That happened with a friend of mine many years ago when my then-girlfriend and I took her out on her 21st birthday. For her first drink, she chose, with our urging (because it was mild) a Long Island Iced Tea. I got a hint that that might not have been a wise choice when she said, "Are you sure this has alcohol in it? I can't even taste it," and proceeded to pretty much just guzzle it. And yes - that was the beginning of a very messy night.

So, with that in mind, I'd tend to think that it should be something that's very definitely alcohol, just so the person knows full well what s/he's getting into. I don't think I'd go so far as scotch, but maybe a bourbon or some other whiskey, and either straight or with a mild mixer. If that's too strong for them (as it would likely be), then they could maybe switch to something sweeter or milder, but it might be good to give them a bit of a shock first, just so they take it seriously.

I've got this! I'm a hobby mixologist with a full bar in my home and I love trying to find drinks that people not just like, but love! I've had German beer in Germany and Belgian beer in Belgium, attended and hosted wine tastings, and can banter with professional bartenders about flavors and technique (and people keep asking me if I'm a bartender...). Also multiple employees on different shifts and vendors recognize me at my local liquor store and I don't work there, but that... maybe that ain't something so much to be proud of.

If you just want to get drunk, do shots of cheap vodka: you won't care what you're drinking after a few, it's more efficient with respect to calories, bladder capacity, and cost than beer. The rest of this post assumes you want to enjoy your drink.

Beer

Go (with friends!) to a beer bar - a bar whose primary focus is beer - and see if they have a "tasting flight." Ask the bartender (or waitperson, if you're really in the right place) for a flight that spans several different styles of beer. Suggestion: (Witbier, Heffeweizen, IPA, Stout, & Marzen)

Or, if you just want answers:

  • (what most people consider) Beer: Gulden Draak
  • (technically still a) Beer: Lindeman's Lambic - Framboise or Cassis

Wine

Go (with friends!) to a wine tasting at a local vinyard or - better - wine store. Ask if they have a "tasting flight." Getcherself a dark red, rose (pink), and white wine, at least. If you love one of them, try more wines of that type. The wine grapes are different every year they're produced and the wine changes (not always the same way) with every year it's aged, so it's unlikely that any specific wine someone mentions will have the same flavor for you even if you manage to track it down.

Or, if you just want answers: You can't go wrong with Sangue di Giuda, a sweet, sparkling red wine.

Spirits

Go (with friends!) to a good bar - not a dive, and not a nightclub. You may need to do this more than once to get through the list... The following drink list should be able to be made by any real bar, and will give you an intro to the main categories of spirits.

  • Tom Collins (Like it? You might like gin)
  • Whiskey Sour NOTE: "no egg" (Like it? You might like whiskey)
  • Margarita on the rocks NOTE: not frozen, please use real lime juice (Like it? You might like tequila)
  • Mojito (Like it? You might like rum)

I have omitted a vodka-based drink from this list because the purpose of vodka in mixed drinks is to increase the alcohol content, and nothing else. In the case of flavored vodkas (of which every bar will have at least a few... and most nightclubs use to excess) the purpose is to add the desired flavor without diluting the drink... or let people buy shots. Bad- to medium-quality vodka is either used this way, or just done in shots to get drunk. Good vodka is sipped, but you won't often find good sipping vodka in a bar's mixing repertoire because it would usually be a waste. Vodka is not a good first drink.

Or, if you just want answers: Get the Tom Collins and make sure they use fresh, real lemon juice.

Bonus: If you're shopping at a liquor store, check for a pre-mixed cocktail bottle from either Tekeen or Austin Cocktails. They're easy, consistent, not too strong, and delicious.

OVERALL

If you just want answers...

  • at a bar: Tom Collins
  • at home: Lambic fruit beer
  • avoid: Shots, Alcopops
